Process Optimization Suggestion: Streamlining the Packing Process
To enhance efficiency in the carton packing process, we suggest implementing a streamlined approach that will significantly reduce non-productive time and improve workflow.
Proposed Change:

Instead of having two employees manually bundling the pouches into sets of five and then placing them into a box, position a carton directly under the sealing machine and assign one person to feed 25 pouches directly onto the sealing conveyor belt.
Why This is a Better Approach:
Eliminates Unnecessary Handling:
Currently, two employees are engaged in bundling the packets before placing them into the box. This additional step adds time without adding value to the process.
With the new setup, packets can move directly from the sealing machine into the box, removing the need for intermediate bundling.
Reduces Non-Productive Time:
Time spent by employees manually bundling and arranging pouches inside the box is a non-value-added activity.
By feeding packets directly into the conveyor belt, we eliminate unnecessary handling and speed up the packing process.
Increases Throughput & Efficiency:
The sealing machine already processes packets sequentially; this new method aligns with its output, reducing idle time.
The carton can be filled faster and more consistently, leading to smoother workflow management.
Reduces Bottlenecks & Labor Dependence:
By automating the movement of packets into the box, we reduce manual workload, allowing employees to focus on more critical tasks.
This frees up resources that can be redirected to other areas, improving overall warehouse efficiency.
Estimated Impact:
Reduction in wasted time: Eliminates delays from manual bundling.
Faster box filling: Packets move directly from the sealing line into the carton.
More efficient workforce allocation: Frees up at least one employee for other tasks.
